query: How to statistically correct for known biases in NFIP claims data when using it as a proxy for actual flood damage at ZCTA level
sub_questions: What statistical methods exist to correct for insurance selection bias (non-random who-has-insurance) in damage estimation?
How do actuarial science and catastrophe modeling handle known undercounting in claims data?
Has anyone published NFIP penetration rate estimates at sub-county resolution (ZIP, census tract, block group)?
What methods exist for detecting and adjusting for structural breaks in insurance claims time series?
Are there published bias correction frameworks for combining multiple biased damage sources (NFIP + FEMA IA + SBA) into a less-biased composite?
gaps: No published application of Heckman/IPW to NFIP selection bias for damage estimation at ZCTA level
Private flood insurance market share data unavailable at sub-state geographic resolution
No published composite framework combining NFIP + FEMA IA + SBA into bias-corrected damage estimate
Cat model adjustment factors (AIR, RMS) are proprietary and not published at ZCTA resolution
NFIP data quality issues (71% missing documentation, 50% PIVOT errors) affect reliability of any correction
